chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whatever affliction befalls you, it is on account of what your hands have wrought.' He said: 'It is [the first part], and [the second part] 'and He pardons most'.'
I said, 'I did not mean this. What is your view of what afflicted Ali and those like him from the People of his Household (peace be upon them) from that [affliction]?'
So he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to repent to Allah seventy times a day, even without having sinned.'

key_terms.مِنْ غَيْرِ ذَنْبٍ: without sin / from without having sinned

ai.seo_question: Why did Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) repent seventy times a day if he was free from sin?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the theological nuance of Quran 42:30, distinguishing between the general principle that afflictions result from human deeds and the specific, elevated status of the Imams, whose sufferings are often acts of divine pardon rather than punishment for sin. It underscores the concept of 'sabr' (patience) and spiritual elevation through suffering, concluding with the Prophetic precedent of constant repentance (tawbah) despite sinlessness, which highlights humility and the continuous need for divine connection.
